persona.title: PhD Candidate — Aerospace Engineering
bio: Aerospace engineer finishing a PhD at Politecnico di Torino, where my work sits at the intersection of human factors, knowledge engineering, and flight simulation.

I am drawn to complexity — the steeper the learning curve, the more engaged I become. Throughout my academic path I have shifted research focus more than once, each time diving deep into unfamiliar territory, and I see that adaptability as one of my strongest assets.
I tend to be analytical and patient, both at work and outside it. I value the effort behind results as much as the results themselves, and I bring that same care to every commitment I take on.
I am now looking for roles — in R&D or research — where curiosity is a job requirement and no two problems look the same.

skillAreas.items: I am proficient in Python, MATLAB. Minor experience with web programming and database management.
I do have experience with productivity tools, including MS Office, Google Docs. I am also familiar with LaTeX, Overleaf, and Git.

Hands-on experience with NLP pipelines (text classification, speech-to-text with Whisper) and ontology modelling (OWL/RDF, Protégé) applied to aerospace research. Basic familiarity with graph databases (Neo4j).

Design and execution of human-in-the-loop experiments in an A320 full-flight simulator environment. Experience with eye-tracking systems (Tobii), multi-modal data acquisition and fusion, and pilot-based test protocols.

education.funding: PNRR — DM 352 | Industrial partner: Leonardo S.p.A.
education.note: Development of knowledge-based support systems for pilot behavioural monitoring on the civilian flight deck, oriented to reduced-crew operations. Ontology-driven procedural modeling and multimodal pilot activity recognition validated through simulator-based flight testing.
